title: Making the Case
grammarNote: Formal argumentation relies on contrastive and causal connectors — 'sin embargo' and 'no obstante' (however), 'en cambio' (on the other hand), 'por lo tanto' (therefore), and 'debido a' (due to) — to link reasons and conclusions smoothly. The concessive 'aunque' splits its meaning by mood: 'aunque es caro' (indicative) states a known fact ('even though it is expensive'), while 'aunque sea caro' (subjunctive) concedes a hypothetical ('even if it turns out to be expensive'). Hedges like 'en principio' and 'hasta cierto punto' soften a claim without abandoning it.

phrases.target: Propongo que trabajemos desde casa dos días
phrases.native: I propose that we work from home two days
phrases.phonetic: pro-PON-go keh tra-bah-HEH-mos DES-deh KAH-sah dos DEE-as
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Proponer que' is the standard formal-register verb for opening a proposal in a meeting; it triggers the subjunctive like other will/suggestion verbs.

exampleSentence.target: Propongo que trabajemos desde casa dos días por semana.
exampleSentence.native: I propose that we work from home two days a week.

phrases.grammarNote: 'Trabajemos' is the regular -ar subjunctive of 'trabajar' in the nosotros form, following the -emos pattern.
phrases.memoryHook: Think of 'proponer' as 'pro' (forward) + 'poner' (to put) — you're putting an idea forward for the group.

phrases.target: Aunque es caro, ahorra tiempo de traslado
phrases.native: Although it's expensive, it saves commute time
phrases.phonetic: ah-OON-keh es KAH-ro, ah-OR-rah TYEM-poh deh tras-lah-DOH
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Aunque' with the indicative ('es caro') states a fact the speaker accepts as true, not a hypothetical.

exampleSentence.target: Aunque es caro instalar el sistema, ahorra tiempo de traslado.
exampleSentence.native: Although it's expensive to install the system, it saves commute time.

phrases.grammarNote: Compare 'aunque es caro' (indicative, known fact) with 'aunque sea caro' (subjunctive, conceded hypothetical) — same connector, different commitment to the truth.
phrases.memoryHook: When 'aunque' is followed by a plain present-tense fact, think 'even though, and I know it for sure'.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: Although it's expensive, it saves commute time
practiceItems.answer: Aunque es caro, ahorra tiempo de traslado

practiceItems.prompt: Aunque es caro, ___ tiempo de traslado.
¿Vale la pena el gasto aunque sea costoso?
practiceItems.answer: Aunque es caro, ahorra tiempo de traslado

phrases.native: Even if it turns out to be expensive, we should try it
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Aunque' with the subjunctive ('sea caro') concedes a hypothetical the speaker isn't sure of, softening the objection.

exampleSentence.target: Aunque sea caro al principio, deberíamos intentarlo este trimestre.
exampleSentence.native: Even if it turns out to be expensive at first, we should try it this quarter.

phrases.grammarNote: 'Sea' signals the concession is hypothetical, not confirmed; this is the same irregular subjunctive of 'ser' from earlier lessons.
phrases.memoryHook: When 'aunque' is followed by the subjunctive, think 'even if it should turn out to be...' — the outcome is still uncertain.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: Even if it turns out to be expensive, we should try it

phrases.target: Entiendo tu punto; sin embargo, hay otra opción
phrases.native: I understand your point; however, there's another option
phrases.phonetic: en-tee-EN-doh too POON-toh; seen em-BAR-go, ai OH-trah op-see-ON
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Sin embargo' (however) is the most common formal-register contrastive connector, used to acknowledge a point before countering it courteously.

exampleSentence.target: Entiendo tu punto sobre el costo; sin embargo, hay otra opción más barata.
exampleSentence.native: I understand your point about the cost; however, there's another, cheaper option.

phrases.grammarNote: 'Sin embargo' can open a new sentence or follow a semicolon; it never takes the subjunctive itself, only the connector between two independent clauses.
phrases.memoryHook: Literally 'without embargo/blockage' — the conversation isn't blocked, it just turns in another direction.
